## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect needs fixing: `refresh_fingerprints` overwrites the stored fingerprint of a tracked file that was edited by hand, which defeats the edit detection the PR description relies on.

## Changes
The pull request adds `refresh_fingerprints` and `register_new_files` to `app/integrity.py`. Both functions write fingerprints for the given names into the JSON manifest. It also adds `tests/test_integrity.py`, which covers both helpers.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — refresh_fingerprints re-blesses hand-edited tracked files — If a tracked file was edited by hand and you call `refresh_fingerprints(root, manifest, ["tracked.txt", "new.txt"])`, line 17 replaces the stored digest with the edited content's digest, and `verify` then returns True. The PR body says "Existing fingerprints let verification detect hand-edited tracked files." The refresh test at tests/test_integrity.py:44 passes only an unchanged tracked file, so it cannot catch the overwrite. — A refresh run after adding new files silently hides tampering with any tracked file named in the same call. — Fix: Skip names already in `entries` as `register_new_files` does at `app/integrity.py:24`, or document that refresh re-approves current content; then extend `test_refresh_registers_new_files_and_keeps_unchanged_entries` with an edited tracked file.
